title: רב המנונא

paragraphs: Rav Hamnuna. Tosafot, Eruvin 63a, writes that there were two: one Rav’s student and one Rav Chisda’s student (see below what I shall write proving this). He sat before Rav Adda bar Achva. Rabbi Acha bar Adda said: Rav Hamnuna said in Rav’s name. He sat before Rabbi Acha bar Azza. In Rabbi Assi’s name: Jerusalem Talmud, Kiddushin chapter 2. Rav Bibi (see Rav Pappa below). Rav Huna was his teacher. There in Eruvin (see below): Rav Huna said in Rav Hamnuna’s name. It appears that this is the earlier Rav Hamnuna, Rav’s student, who also learned from Rabbi Chanina. The second Rav Hamnuna was Rav Huna’s student and Rav Chisda’s student-colleague. One cannot say: since Rav Huna was Rav’s student and Rav Hamnuna likewise Rav’s student, perhaps Rav Hamnuna was Rav Huna’s student-colleague. This is not so: when Rav Hamnuna was before Rav Huna he had no wife (see above, Rav Huna turned his face away from him). How could his student-colleague have had no wife? Necessarily there were two: the second was his student, and the earlier his colleague, both Rav’s students. Rav Huna bar Sechora before him. Rabbi Zeira said, “Rav Hamnuna asked me this matter”—it should read “conveyed it to me indirectly,” as in N.Y.; see his entry. He told Rabbi Zeira, “Stay on your feet until you tell me”: Zevachim 105b. Rav Zeira in Rabbi Hamnuna’s name: Jerusalem Talmud, Kilayim 4:4; end of Horayot chapter 1. Rabbi Zerika in his name. Rabbi Hamnuna said, “Rabbi Chanina taught me this matter, and it is as dear as all my learning”: end of Menachot chapter 2; Rashi explains: he gave me understanding and taught me. Rav Chisda and Rav Hamnuna sat at a meal. Rav Hamnuna took and blessed; Rav Chisda asked, “Does the master not hold …?” He answered …; Rav Chisda said, “Who would give us iron legs so we could attend you?” Berakhot 41b. He spoke to Rav Chisda, or Rav Chisda spoke to him: Shabbat 97a. Rabbi Tavi in his name. Before Rav Yehudah; Rav Yehudah said, “You are Hamnuna? Enter the study house, for you make your teacher wiser”: Shevuot 34. Rav Yehudah bar Natan with him. Rabbi Yonah in his name. Rabbi Yosef sat before Rav Hamnuna: Ketubbot 50, beginning of side b. Tosafot writes that this implies Rav Yosef was lesser than Rav Hamnuna, whereas Kiddushin chapter 1, 25, implies Rav Hamnuna was Rav Chisda’s student, and Rabbi Yosef Rav Chisda’s colleague. Necessarily there were two Rav Hamnunas. (Requires examination: Rav Chisda addressed him as “master”; see his entry, that he was Rav Chisda’s student-colleague.) Rav Yosef said: this matter was a question for Rav Chisda, and Rav Hamnuna resolved it for him. Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha in his name. He said to Rav Nachman: Zevachim 103a. Rav Nachman said to Rava, “Now that you have objected and Rav Hamnuna in Sura has objected, we shall not act”: Bava Batra 31b. Rabbi Nicha bar Sava in his name; Rabbi Salla in his name. He objected to Ulla: Chullin 34b. He sat before Ulla and raised difficulties in the teaching. Ulla said, “What a man!”—how great he is—“if only Harpanya were not his town”—its people lack established lineage. He was ashamed. He asked, “Where did you pay your poll tax?” He answered, “To Pum Nehara.” He said, “Then you are from Pum Nehara”: end of Yevamot chapter 1, 17a. In Ulla’s name: Shabbat 10b. Rav Pappa sat behind Rabbi Bibi, who sat before Rav Hamnuna (see his entry). Rava saw Rav Hamnuna prolonging his prayer and said, “They leave eternal life …”: Shabbat 10a. Sefer Beer Sheva, Horayot chapter 3, writes: it is very difficult—how does it object from Rava against Rav Hamnuna, since Hamnuna was greater than Rava? Hamnuna was Rav Chisda’s student-colleague, while Rava was Rav Chisda’s full student. In Sanhedrin chapter 1, 17b, “They say in Rav’s house” means Rav Hamnuna. Tosafot objects: in Yevamot 83b, it means Rav Huna (see his entry). Moreover, how can Rav Huna report Rav Hamnuna, since Rav Chisda was Rav Huna’s student and Rav Hamnuna Rav Chisda’s student, Kiddushin chapter 1, 25? Yet we find Rav Hamnuna studied before Rav: Eruvin 84; there, 54a, Rav said to Rav Hamnuna, “My son, if you have means, do yourself good”; Bava Kamma 106: Rav Hamnuna, Rav’s student. Tosafot there, 75,end of side a: how did Rav Huna use “They say in Rav’s house” of Rav Hamnuna, his student’s student—meaning, Chisda was Huna’s student and Hamnuna Chisda’s—as appears in chapter Hadar, 63a? Thus “the elders of Rav’s house” means Rav Huna (see his entry). It is puzzling that it says Hamnuna was his student’s student in Hadar, since Tosafot there wrote that this is the second R.H. [ר״ה, as printed]. Rabbah came to Sura; Rav Hamnuna told him: Bava Metzia 6b. Rabbah met Rav Hamnuna and put a mishnah to him: Sanhedrin 61a. Rabbah bar Rav Adda in his name. The exilarch asked him, “What does ‘And the Lord’s holy one …’ mean?” Shabbat 119a. Rav Sheshet said, “I say thus, and Hamnuna says …”: Eruvin 67a. The elders of Nezunya did not attend Rav Chisda’s lectures. He told Rav Hamnuna, “Go and discipline them ….” They asked him about a slave whom his master castrated …; he did not have the answer. They asked his name. He said, “Hamnuna.” They said, “Your name is not Hamnuna but Karnuna.” Rashi: one who sits at corners. Tosafot: Hamnuna means cham nuna, hot fish; he is instead kar nuna, cold fish. Ritva explains Hamnuna as a faithful peg in the study house, the opposite of Karnuna: Kiddushin 25. When Rav Hamnuna died, hailstones descended from heaven. When Rav Hamnuna and Rabbah bar Rav Huna died, they brought them up there. At the bridge, the camels stopped. An Arab asked why. They told him, “The sages honor one another; one says, ‘Let the master enter first ….’” He said, “In my judgment a man who is a man’s son”—Rabbah bar Rav Huna—“should enter first.” Rabbah bar Rav Huna’s camel passed; that Arab’s molars and teeth fell out, because he disparaged Rav Hamnuna: Moed Katan 25. Perhaps this is the second Rav Hamnuna, whom Rav Chisda praised to Rav Huna as a great man, Kiddushin chapter 1, 29b; it says there Rav Huna turned his face away from him because he had no wife. Rav Hamnuna’s burial cave is in the town where he lived, Charta of Argiz: Rashi, Shabbat 19b. The Arukh writes it is a town about a parasang from Baghdad, and it was Rav’s place, there. Thus it appears there were two Rav Hamnunas: one buried in the Land of Israel, one in Babylonia. So Rashi, Berakhot 54,end of side b,s.v. Bagdata’ah: his town Baghdad is Babylonia’s important city since Babylon was destroyed (see above, Rav Chana of Baghdad; see Benjamin’s travels). G.A.Y. writes: Rabbah bar Rav Huna, Rav Hamnuna, Rav Huna and Rav Chananel were buried in Kefar Alma; it is called the Babylonians’ cave (see Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh).
